page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-48 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the arm64 processor architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384 GB of system memory, delivering a consistent memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This high memory allocation targets applications that demand substantial working memory capacity relative to compute thread count.

The hardware configuration contains no bundled local storage and zero graphics processing units. All operating system and application storage requirements must be met using external network-attached volumes. In addition, the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated routing infrastructure or separately provisioned public IPs for internet-facing connectivity. Running on the 64-bit ARM architecture requires all operational software, runtimes, and dependencies to be compatible with arm64 binaries.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the n4a-highmem-48 provides significant memory capacity on energy-efficient ARM hardware, offering favorable cost-to-resource characteristics for workloads that do not require x86-specific instruction sets. The server profile is suited for memory-intensive tasks including in-memory databases, distributed key-value caches, large search indexes, memory-bound ETL pipelines, and high-throughput data processing systems.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-48 is an arm64 compute instance offering 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Built for memory-heavy operations, the instance features no local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached persistent storage for all disk I/O. The deployment model includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, making network address translation or reserved IPs necessary for public routing. The underlying ARM architecture provides strong cost efficiency and density for workloads optimized for multi-core arm64 execution. Due to its balanced compute-to-memory allocation, the n4a-highmem-48 is aligned with production in-memory databases, Redis caches, analytical processing engines, and distributed memory-bound applications.
